## Lab overview

Today we are going to do the following:

(1) go through fitting the multiple linear regression model for the baby birth weight data in R;
(2) create the plots from the class notes to examine conditions for multiple linear regression in R;
(4) take a first pass at creating a slide deck in RMarkdown (via ioslides)

# Multiple linear regression (MLR) in R

## Fitting a MLR model {.smaller}

The advantage of creating your presentation within R Markdown is that you have everything you need in one place - changes to code and plots will automatically update when you knit your document (just like in other R labs).

The code below fits the full model for the baby birth weight data we discussed in class. Additional variables are separated by a '+' sign.

```{r tidy=TRUE}
m_full <- lm(bwt ~ gestation + age + parity + smoke + height + weight,
             data = babies)
```

## MLR model fit summary {.smaller}

<!-- THE FOLLOWING WILL NOT PRINT ON YOUR SLIDES BUT YOU SHOULD READ IT: On this slide we are just printing the summary output for the full model that you fit in the previous R chunk. Notice that sometimes the output is too long to fit nicely on the slide. -->

```{r}
## print model summary 
summary(m_full)
```

# Checking model conditions

```{r include=FALSE}
## get all the information you need to make diagnostic plots together in one data frame
## this approach generally works even with other data sets

## pulls the data for all explanatory variables
m_no_age_fit <- m_no_age$model

## creates another column of residuals
m_no_age_fit$residuals <- m_no_age$residuals
## creates another column of fitted values
m_no_age_fit$fitted = m_no_age$fitted.values
## creates another column for order of collection
m_no_age_fit$order <- 1:nrow(m_no_age_fit)

## take a look at the first few rows of m_no_age_fit
head(m_no_age_fit)
```

## Residuals versus model fit

Example code to use for remainder of plots

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', out.width='90%', out.height='90%'}
# create residuals vs fitted plot and assign to res_plot

res_plot <- ggplot(data = m_no_age_fit, aes(x=fitted, y=residuals)) + 
  geom_point(color="lightblue") + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) + 
  xlab("Fitted Values") + 
  ylab("Residuals")
res_plot
```
